sections.heading: Dayananda Sagar University vs Institute of Clinical Research for Healthcare PG: which is better in 2026
paragraphs: This page cannot name a current placement winner. ICRI's latest recorded year is 2016, with an average of ₹7 lakh and a highest of ₹8 lakh, which is older than 2020.

sections.heading: Fees: what our records show
paragraphs: Dayananda Sagar University has a recorded year-wise total of ₹1 lakh. Treat this as a recorded year fee, not a confirmed programme total, until you check the official circular for the exact healthcare postgraduate programme.
ICRI has no fee row on this page. Do not guess the fee, and do not copy a figure from another ICRI campus. Use the official Bengaluru notice.

sections.heading: Placements compared
paragraphs: DSU has no placement row on this page. Ask the university for its latest official postgraduate placement report.

ICRI's latest recorded year here is 2016. Because that is older than 2020, this page does not treat it as a current flagship result. Inventory also flags that this row may be tied to an executive-style programme, so match the programme name on any official report you use.

sections.heading: Admission and eligibility
paragraphs: Neither side has an entrance exam listed in our records on this page. Healthcare postgraduate admissions may use a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject, a university test or an interview.
Read the current official admissions page of each institute for eligibility and duration.

sections.heading: Location and campus
paragraphs: Both are listed in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on different campuses. Confirm the teaching location for the exact programme you will join.
A Bengaluru label is not enough if internships or clinical postings happen on another site.

sections.heading: Verdict: who should pick which college
paragraphs: On this page, DSU is the only side with a recorded year fee, at ₹1 lakh, and ICRI is the only side with a placement row, which is too old to use as a current figure.
Get both official fee circulars and a recent official placement report before you decide.
Do not use the 2016 ICRI row as a forecast for a 2026 graduating class.
